name: Sunaina Devi
story: Sunaina learned Mithila painting from her mother and grandmother, painting wedding walls before ever touching paper. Today she leads a women's collective of 30 artists and teaches the Kachni fine-line style to a new generation.

name: Gurmeet Kaur
story: Gurmeet revived her grandmother's bagh phulkari patterns after they nearly disappeared to machine embroidery. Her cooperative now supplies hand-embroidered dupattas to buyers across India.

name: Mohan Lal Kumhar
story: A third-generation potter, Mohan Lal shapes clay-free quartz bodies and hand-paints Persian florals in cobalt. He runs workshops near Amber to keep the delicate, low-fire craft alive.

name: Ayesha Begum
story: Ayesha has embroidered chikankari from her home in old Lucknow since she was fourteen, mastering the raised murri and phanda stitches. She now coordinates work for a group of forty women artisans.

name: Ramesh Verma
story: Ramesh casts and engraves brass lamps and ritual vessels used in the Ganga aarti, a craft his family has practised beside the ghats for generations.
